svg.text: The SMART Study · set-up guide
Testing the "Block apps" step
Version A · iPhone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your child's phone
Already have App Limits? Keep them, and add this one
alongside.
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits → Add
Limit.
2. Tick these categories one by one: Social, Games,
Entertainment, Creativity, Productivity & Finance,
Education, Health & Fitness, Shopping & Food, Travel
and Other. Work down the list so you don't miss one.
3. Leave Information & Reading and Utilities unticked,
and don't tick Websites. Your child's phone needs
these two for getting on the web at all. The
websites step then limits the web to the sites on
the list.
4. Do not tick "All Apps & Categories" at the top. It
looks like a shortcut, but it also cuts off web
access, which undoes the websites step.
5. Tap Next and set the limit to 0 minutes.
6. Turn on Block at End of Limit. Without it there's an
"Ignore Limit" button and nothing holds.

svg.text: Version A · Android phone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
Already have downtime at bedtime? This replaces it with
downtime all day. The apps you allow back next will then
work at night too. If you want them off at night, email us
and we'll help.
1. Open Family Link. It opens on Screen time (bottom
left).
2. Tap Schedules. Turn on Downtime, and leave School
time off.
3. Tap Weekly schedule, then Mon. Check Downtime ON is
switched on, set Start time to 12:00 and End time to
11:59, tick Apply to all days of the week and tap
Done. Every day should now show 12:00–11:59, so
downtime covers the whole day.

svg.text: Version B · iPhone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your child's phone
Already have App Limits? Keep them, and add this one
alongside.
This is the step that does the work. One limit blocks
whole categories of apps, including any your child
installs later. In the next step you allow back the few
your child needs.
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits → Add
Limit.
2. Tick every category except two. Leave Information &
Reading and Utilities unticked: the phone needs them
to open any website, and Step 6 limits the web
separately.
– Don't tick "All Apps & Categories" at the top, or
Websites at the bottom. They look like shortcuts,
but they cut off the web too.
3. Tap Next. The top of the screen should say 10
Categories. If it says a different number, go back
and check the ticks.
4. Set the time to 0 minutes and tap Add.
5. Turn on Block at End of Limit. Without it, your
child gets an Ignore Limit button and nothing holds.
Nothing is deleted. Apps, photos and messages stay on the
phone, just locked. You can change any of this later with
your code.
Need one app from a ticked category, such as a map or a
school app? Don't untick the whole category. Allow back just
that app in the next step.

svg.text: Version B · Android phone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
Already have downtime at bedtime? This replaces it with
downtime all day. The apps you allow back next will then
work at night too. If you want them off at night, email us
and we'll help.
This is the step that does the work. Family Link doesn't
group apps into categories, so the way to block
everything at once, including apps installed later, is
downtime for the whole day. It sounds drastic, but it's
only the first half: in the next step you allow back the
few apps your child needs.
1. Open Family Link. It opens on Screen time (bottom
left). Tap Schedules.
2. Turn on Downtime. Leave School time off.
3. Tap Weekly schedule, then Mon. Check Downtime ON is
switched on, set Start time to 12:00 and End time to
11:59, tick Apply to all days of the week and tap
Done.
4. Every day should now show 12:00–11:59. That means
downtime covers the whole day.
Your child's phone will lock, apart from calls, until you
finish the next step. That's expected. Nothing is deleted:
apps, photos and messages stay on the phone.
Need another app? You can allow it back in the next step
too.

svg.text: Version C · iPhone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your child's phone
Already have App Limits? Keep them, and add this one
alongside.
This is the step that does the work. You block the three
categories that hold the apps children spend most time
on: social media, games and video. That includes any
your child installs later.
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits → Add
Limit.
2. Tick three categories: Social, Games and
Entertainment. Leave the rest unticked.
– Don't tick "All Apps & Categories" at the top. It
looks like a shortcut, but it blocks everything, the
web included.
3. Tap Next. The top of the screen should say 3
Categories.
4. Set the time to 0 minutes and tap Add.
5. Turn on Block at End of Limit. Without it, your
child gets an Ignore Limit button and nothing holds.
Nothing is deleted. Apps, photos and messages stay on the
phone, just locked. You can change any of this later with
your code.
Messaging apps such as WhatsApp are in Social, so they're
blocked too. You'll allow WhatsApp back in the next step.

svg.text: Version C · Android phone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
Already blocked some apps? Keep them blocked. If you have
downtime at bedtime, you can keep that too.
This is the step that does the work. You block the
social media, game and video apps on your child's phone.
These hold the apps children spend most time on.
1. Open Family Link on Screen time and tap Time limits,
then App limits.
2. Go down the list. Tap each social media, game or
video app, such as YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat or
Roblox, and choose Block.
3. Leave everything else as it is. You don't need
downtime in this version.
New apps can't be installed without your approval once
you've done Step 7, so nothing new slips in.
Nothing is deleted. A blocked app stays on the phone, just
locked.

svg.text: Version C · Android phone · Step 5
Allow back the apps your child
needs
10 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
Already set limits on some apps? Change the ones below to
Unlimited time. Leave the rest as they are.
In this version only the apps you chose are blocked, so
this is a quick check.
1. In App limits, check that none of these says
Blocked: Messages, WhatsApp, Google Maps, [Life360],
Weather, [Moodle], [your child's school app], Camera
and Clock. If one does, tap it and choose Unlimited
time.
2. Set Google Chrome to Unlimited time too, so the
websites in the next step open.
If your child needs another app. You can allow back one
more app yourself, in the same way: for example one their
school or a club uses. Please use your judgement. Will they
need it most weeks? Does it have videos, a feed, games, or
chat with people they don't know? If it has any of those,
leave it blocked. If you're not sure, leave it blocked and
ask us. Please tell us about any app you add, at
smartphonestudy@public.io. If other families need it too,
we'll add it to the guide for everyone.
Version D · iPhone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your child's phone
Already have App Limits? Keep them, and add this one
alongside.
This is the step that does the work. One limit blocks
whole categories of apps, including any your child
installs later. You tick them in two goes: the three
that matter most, then the rest.
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits → Add
Limit.
2. First, tick Social, Games and Entertainment. These
hold the apps children spend most time on: social
media, games and video.
3. Then tick the rest, apart from Information & Reading
and Utilities. The phone needs those two to open any
website, and Step 6 limits the web separately.
– Don't tick "All Apps & Categories" at the top, or
Websites at the bottom. They look like shortcuts,
but they cut off the web too.
4. Tap Next. The top of the screen should say 10
Categories.
5. Set the time to 0 minutes and tap Add.
6. Turn on Block at End of Limit. Without it, your
child gets an Ignore Limit button and nothing holds.
Nothing is deleted. Apps, photos and messages stay on the
phone, just locked. You can change any of this later with
your code.
Need one app from a ticked category, such as a map or a
school app? Don't untick the whole category. Allow back just
that app in the next step.

svg.text: Version D · Android phone · Step 4
Block apps
5 minutes · on your phone, in Family Link
Already have downtime at bedtime? This replaces it with
downtime all day. The apps you allow back next will then
work at night too. If you want them off at night, email us
and we'll help.
This is the step that does the work. You do it in two
goes: first the apps that matter most, then everything
else.
1. First, block social media, games and video. In
Family Link, tap Time limits, then App limits. Tap
each social media, game or video app, such as
YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat or Roblox, and choose
Block.
2. Then block everything else, with downtime for the
whole day. Go back to Screen time and tap Schedules.
Turn on Downtime and leave School time off.
3. Tap Weekly schedule, then Mon. Check Downtime ON is
switched on, set Start time to 12:00 and End time to
11:59, tick Apply to all days of the week and tap
Done.
4. Every day should now show 12:00–11:59. That means
downtime covers the whole day.
Your child's phone will lock, apart from calls, until you
finish the next step. That's expected. Nothing is deleted.
Need another app? You can allow it back in the next step
too.
